html:
SMTO-CFG-0089 — SMTO couldn't save turning on a Skill, so it didn't use it

GUID: 3774a3e2-2fe2-5975-a8f9-9bccbd3b5a7e
Slug: capability-activation-persist-failed
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • SMTO tried to turn on a Skill for this Task but couldn't confirm the change was saved. To stay safe, SMTO won't use a Skill until that change is saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Task, look for a Capabilities activated for this request note after this message. If that note appears, the change was saved after all and you don't need to do anything.
  2. Open System Health and check Storage and persistence for warnings. SMTO couldn't save the change, which can mean its storage is full or not responding.
  3. Once storage looks healthy, ask SMTO to continue the Task. With saving working again, SMTO can turn on the Skill and record it safely.

What success looks like

  • A Capabilities activated for this request note appears and the Task keeps working with the Skill.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details and what System Health shows to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder to make room; it holds your conversations and Tasks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Committing a dynamic capability activation failed, so the change was not persisted and no unsaved capability may execute (capability_activation.persist_failed); this retained label has no direct current producer.

What this means

  • This retained persistence-failure kind has no direct current producer; activation transactions restore the prior in-memory state and rethrow on failure rather than publish this specific label. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • This retained persistence-failure kind has no direct current producer; activation transactions restore the prior in-memory state and rethrow on failure rather than publish this specific label.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual transaction outcome and current accepted epoch; the retained label alone does not identify a disk or database fault.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the activation transaction outcome and the run's current_capability_selection epoch (request in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_activation.py restores the prior in-memory state and rethrows on failure). Resolve the underlying storage or transaction error from the Server log before any new activation, and never execute a capability that is not in the committed selection.
  • Inspect the existing activation result and fix its established persistence problem before any new activation; never execute an uncommitted capability.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • Authoritative saved state confirms exactly which capabilities are active.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
